name: Instruction and acknowledgement
purpose: Present an approved work instruction (text, parameter values, diagrams, safety/PPE notes, link to governing SOP) and capture that the operator read it or performed it.
config_options: rich text with placeholders bound to formula/process parameters
controlled images, diagrams or video from a versioned media library
acknowledgement type: read-only vs confirm-performed
signature level: none, performer, performer plus verifier
link to governing SOP/document number
approved translations per language
display conditions (e.g. only for first batch of campaign)
engine_enforced_rules: text and media are rendered only from the approved MBR version; nothing can be edited at run time
placeholders resolve from bound, approved parameters, never from free text typed at execution
acknowledgement stored with authenticated user and server timestamp
SOP link resolves to the version effective at execution and that version number is written into the record
translations are part of the approved MBR version; changing a translation requires a new MBR version
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.100(a)-(b) and 211.186(b)(9) (complete manufacturing and control instructions); EU GMP Chapter 4 (processing instructions)

name: Numeric data entry / process parameter record
purpose: Record a measured or observed numeric value (process parameter, reading, count) with its unit and evaluate it against approved limits.
config_options: label and parameter code
data type (decimal/integer) and unit from the controlled UoM catalogue
precision as decimal places or significant figures
target plus tiered limits (alert/action or in-process/acceptance), inclusive or exclusive bounds
criticality class (CPP, KPP, non-critical)
allowed sources: device, automation, manual
verification requirement
permit not-applicable (with reason) or not
mandatory comment when out of limit
engine_enforced_rules: value stored with its unit at the precision entered; conversions only via the UoM service with dimension checking
limit comparison uses the compendial rounding rule attached to the limit, not a rounded stored value
out-of-limit values are kept, flagged and raise an exception; they can't be silently replaced
manual entry of a value classed as critical requires an accuracy check (second-person verification, double entry or device capture); the configuration can pick which one but cannot pick none
corrections preserve the original and require a reason
regulatory_basis: EU GMP Annex 11 sections 5 and 6 (built-in checks, accuracy check of critical manually entered data); 21 CFR 211.188(b); 21 CFR 11.10(e)

name: Choice, pass/fail and checklist
purpose: Capture categorical observations (yes/no, pass/fail, selection from a controlled list) singly or as a checklist.
config_options: controlled value set per question
expected (passing) answer(s)
single vs multi-select
per-item comment or photo on unexpected answer
checklist item library reuse
signature/verification per item or per checklist
engine_enforced_rules: no answer is pre-filled or defaulted; each item needs a positive act by the user
an unexpected answer raises an exception and blocks dependent steps as configured
each checklist item is stored individually with its answer, not as a single 'all OK' flag
value sets are versioned master data; the record stores the value, not a pointer that could later change meaning
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.100(b), 211.188(b); FDA Data Integrity Q&A (2018) on attributable and contemporaneous records

name: Free text and date/time entry
purpose: Capture observations, remarks and externally sourced event times (e.g. time printed on an instrument ticket) that do not fit a structured field.
config_options: maximum length, mandatory/optional
controlled phrase suggestions
date/time format and time zone display
plausibility window for entered event times (e.g. between step start and now)
engine_enforced_rules: user-entered event times are stored as data and never replace the server timestamp of the entry
entered dates in the future or outside the batch window are rejected
MBR design check warns when free text is used where a structured, limit-checked field exists (to avoid 'paper on glass')
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 11.10(e); EU GMP Annex 11 section 5; EU GMP Chapter 4

name: Automated equipment phase / Level-2 data exchange
purpose: Invoke or supervise an equipment-executed phase (DCS/PLC/SCADA/skid) in ISA-88 terms: send setpoints from the approved formula, start/confirm the phase, and collect actual values, totals, events and alarms into the record.
config_options: equipment class and Level-2 phase or recipe identifier
mapping of formula/process parameters to setpoint tags
values to collect (actuals, totals, min/max over window, end-of-phase report)
sampling interval and time window
acceptance limits on collected values
alarm/event classes to import and which require review
manual fallback sub-procedure if interface is down (optional)
engine_enforced_rules: setpoints come only from approved formula values (or operator edits inside an approved range, verified); downloads are read back and compared before start
every imported value keeps provenance: source system, tag, device ID, source timestamp
interface loss, stale data or read-back mismatch raises an exception; fallback to manual entry is allowed only via the MBR-defined fallback path and is flagged in the record
when automation performed the operation, one person confirms correct performance; that confirmation is mandatory
alarms configured as review-relevant cannot be dropped from the review-by-exception report
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.68(a)-(c) (automatic equipment; input/output checked for accuracy; one-person check of automated operation); EU GMP Annex 11 section 5 (checks on data exchanged electronically between systems); ISA-88/ISA-95 Level 2-3 boundary

name: Weighing and dispensing (gravimetric)
purpose: Dispense a component into labelled containers for a specific batch to a calculated target within tolerance, with scale integration and status checks.
config_options: item and target source (formula line after scaling/potency adjustment)
tolerance absolute or relative, symmetric or asymmetric
method: net with tare, gross, weigh-by-difference, multi-container accumulation, whole-container issue
allowed scale classes / booths; minimum-weight rules
lot selection policy (FEFO/FIFO proposal, override with reason)
environmental prerequisites for the booth
container type and label template
verification: second person or automated-equipment single check
engine_enforced_rules: lot must be released, unexpired/within retest, correct item; identity confirmed by scanning the source container

scale must be calibrated, have a passed periodic performance check, and suit the target (target at or above the scale's minimum weight; readability fine enough for the tolerance) otherwise the step is blocked
weight captured from the scale interface; manual keying only via flagged fallback with mandatory verification
label generated from system data (content per 211.101(b), plus a unique container ID); no handwritten or typed labels
out-of-tolerance weight can't be accepted without exception; the accumulated quantity per item is reconciled against the target

second-person examination of each dispensed container (released status, correct weight, correct identification) unless weighing was done by qualified automated equipment, in which case one person checks
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.101(a)-(c), 211.68, 211.84, 211.188(b); EU GMP Chapter 5 (dispensing of starting materials); USP <41>/<1251> balance minimum weight concept for analytical balances

name: Volumetric or flow-metered liquid dispensing
purpose: Dispense or transfer liquids (granulating fluid, solvents, coating liquids, WFI, bulk solution) by volume or mass with optional density/temperature conversion.
config_options: measurement principle: flow meter totaliser, calibrated vessel, load cell
conversion by density (from specification, lot CoA or measured) and temperature compensation
tolerance
source point (tank, WFI use point, container) and destination
verification requirement
engine_enforced_rules: conversions performed only by the calculation engine with dimensional checking (volume x density = mass)
meter/load cell calibration status checked before use
totaliser values read from the device where interfaced; manual readings flagged and verified
density value source recorded (spec constant vs lot-specific vs measured)
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.101(b)-(c), 211.68; EU GMP Chapter 5

name: Material identification and charge-in
purpose: Add dispensed components (or intermediates) to the right equipment in the right order and prove each container was added once to the right batch.
config_options: charge list derived from dispensing or formula
sequence: strict order, free order within a group, or parallel
target equipment/vessel
partial charges and rinse/transfer steps
addition rate or time constraints
verification rule
engine_enforced_rules: each container is scanned; it must belong to this batch and this charge step and not be already consumed
status and expiry are re-checked at the point of use
the step cannot complete until every required container is charged or explicitly handled via exception
manual charge-in requires a different second person to verify; only automated addition reduces this to a single verifying person

name: Formula scaling and quantity adjustment
purpose: Compute batch-specific quantities from the approved formula: scale to actual batch size and adjust for lot potency/assay, water or LOD, salt-to-base factor, and compensating excipient.
config_options: approved batch-size range and scaling rule per line (proportional, fixed, stepwise)
adjustment basis per active (as-is, anhydrous, dried basis, free base)
source attribute for lot values (CoA/LIMS result fields)
compensating item (q.s. filler) and its allowed range
rounding to dispensing resolution
engine_enforced_rules: actual batch size must lie within the approved range of the MBR version
lot-specific values are pulled from quality-approved results, never typed
formulas come from the validated expression library; the computation trace (inputs, versions, result) is stored
compensating adjustments cannot drive any item outside its approved range; total batch mass is re-checked
result is verified by a second person or covered by validated automated calculation plus one-person check
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.101(a), 211.186(b)(3)-(4), 211.68(b); EU GMP Chapter 4 (manufacturing formula)

name: Equipment identification and status check
purpose: Bind a specific equipment unit (or train) to the step and prove it is fit for use; update its logbook automatically.
config_options: required equipment class and capabilities (e.g. working-volume range, tooling type)
list of permitted units or any unit of the class
checks to apply: cleaning status and type (e.g. product-change vs same-product clean), clean-hold expiry, calibration, qualification, preventive maintenance, open work orders
start of dirty-hold timer on release
attributes to record (e.g. line speed setting, change parts)
engine_enforced_rules: unit must be of the required class; wrong class or a failed status check blocks the step
unit ID is written to the batch record and a use entry (product, batch, time, user) to the equipment logbook automatically
a unit in use by another batch or in 'dirty' or 'maintenance' status cannot be bound
after use the unit goes to 'dirty' and its dirty-hold clock starts from server time

name: Room/line status and line clearance
purpose: Confirm, before starting (and at the end of) an operation, that the room/line is free of previous product, documents and printed materials and is in the right status.
config_options: checklist template per room/line type and operation (processing vs packaging)
photo evidence per item
automatic display of previous product/batch in that room/line
performer, verifier and optional QA verification
start-of-batch, end-of-batch and changeover triggers
engine_enforced_rules: steps located in a room/line cannot start until clearance is recorded and verified by a different person
any failed item blocks start and raises an exception
previous product/batch is filled in by the system, not typed
clearance status resets when the batch ends or another batch occupies the room/line
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.130(e) (inspection of packaging and labeling facilities immediately before use, documented in batch record), 211.188(b); EU GMP Chapter 5 (line clearance before packaging and processing)

name: Environmental condition check
purpose: Verify room conditions (temperature, RH, differential pressure, particles) before and/or during a step, from a monitoring system or manual reading.
config_options: parameters and limits per room class/product need (e.g. low RH for moisture-sensitive or effervescent tablets; pressure cascades for cleanrooms)
source: BMS/EMS integration or manual instrument
timing: before start, periodic, or the full step window
action on excursion (block, exception only)
engine_enforced_rules: integrated values carry source timestamp and instrument ID; manual readings are flagged and verified
for window checks the engine pulls the excursion log for the exact step interval and attaches it for review
an excursion always generates an exception; configuration can only choose whether it also blocks
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.42, 211.46; EU GMP Chapter 3; EU GMP Annex 1 (for sterile)

name: Sampling (QC, IPC, retain, micro, stability)
purpose: Take defined samples with unique IDs, labels and chain of custody, and trigger or link laboratory testing.
config_options: sample type and purpose
quantity, container and number of samples
sampling point: location, time or event (start/middle/end, per container, per n units)
sampling plan reference (e.g. stratified locations)
label template
LIMS test/specification mapping
hand-over and receipt confirmation
engine_enforced_rules: system-generated unique sample IDs and labels; the source container/location is scanned
sampler, time and quantity recorded; sample quantity flows into yield/reconciliation
test requests sent to LIMS automatically and results returned against the sample ID
missing or late samples appear as exceptions at batch review

name: In-process control test with repeated readings and statistics
purpose: Generic IPC container for n readings per sample/time point with computed statistics and multi-tier acceptance rules (the tablet and injectable IPC blocks specialise it).
config_options: test type and method reference
n readings per sample, grouping by time point/station/side/nozzle
individual limits absolute or relative to the computed mean
statistics to compute (mean, SD, RSD, min, max, range, counts outside tiers)
acceptance rule types: mean within limits; individuals within limits; at most k outside tier 1 and none outside tier 2
instrument integration
retest rule reference (only per approved procedure)
engine_enforced_rules: statistics computed by the validated engine at full precision; rounding only for comparison/display
every reading retained; excluding a reading needs documented invalidation with reason and verification
a failing result raises an exception; a retest never replaces the original result
instrument ID and calibration status recorded with device-captured readings
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.110(a)-(b) (in-process specifications from process average/variability with suitable statistics), 211.160, 211.188(b); EU GMP Chapter 4 (IPC results in batch record); Ph. Eur. 2.9.5 (tiered relative-to-mean limits)

name: Calculation
purpose: Derive a value (e.g. yield, potency-adjusted amount, weight gain, mean) from recorded data and master data using the approved expression language.
config_options: expression in the sandboxed expression language referencing named inputs
output unit and precision/rounding policy
limits on the result
whether the formula is displayed to the user
verification requirement where not covered by validated automation
engine_enforced_rules: deterministic, side-effect-free evaluation; no scripts, I/O or network access
design-time unit/dimension check and dependency-graph cycle detection
full precision for intermediates; rounding only at limit comparison/reporting
if an input is corrected, the result is recomputed, the old result is preserved and dependent steps are flagged for re-verification
no manual override of a computed value
calculation trace (inputs, versions, output) stored
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.68(b) (formulas/input-output checked for accuracy), 211.103; EU GMP Annex 11 sections 5-6; FDA Data Integrity Q&A (2018) on validating MPCR calculations

name: Timer, hold time and time-limit enforcement
purpose: Measure and enforce minimum and maximum elapsed times between any two recorded events, within a step, across unit procedures, or across batches (e.g. mixing time, drying time, dirty/clean hold, bulk hold, compounding-to-filtration).
config_options: start event and stop event (any step/phase event, equipment status change or material status change)
minimum duration, maximum duration, alert threshold before maximum
scope: within step, across unit procedures, across batches (intermediate hold)
behaviour at maximum: exception only or exception plus block
display of live countdown on operator and supervisor screens
engine_enforced_rules: durations are computed from server timestamps of recorded events, never typed by users
a step guarded by a minimum time cannot complete early
exceeding a maximum always creates an exception; configuration can add blocking but cannot suppress the exception
timers continue independently of client sessions and survive restarts
time-limit values must reference an approved source (validation/hold-time study) in the MBR
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.111 (time limits for each production phase; deviations justified and documented); FDA guidance Sterile Drug Products Produced by Aseptic Processing (2004) on time limits; EU GMP Annex 1 (2022)

name: Verification / witness
purpose: Independent check of a performed action or entered value by a second person, either concurrently (witness) or immediately after (verification).
config_options: target step(s) or fields
mode: concurrent witness within a time window, or subsequent verification
verifier role(s)
what the verifier must actively re-check (re-scan container, view scale display, compare values)
optional stricter independence (e.g. not the same shift lead)
engine_enforced_rules: verifier must be a different authenticated individual from the performer
verification cannot precede the verified action and must show the actual evidence (values, scans, images)
signature meaning recorded as verification

mandatory where regulation requires it (manual charge-in, manual yield calculation, critical manual data entry) and cannot be removed; reduced to a single checking person only when qualified automated equipment performed the operation
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.101(c)-(d), 211.103, 211.68(c), 211.188(b)(11); EU GMP Annex 11 section 6; EU GMP Chapter 4

name: QA hold point / in-process release gate
purpose: Stop the flow until the quality unit reviews evidence and releases (or rejects) an intermediate or the continuation of the batch.
config_options: gate position in the flow
evidence required (IPC results, LIMS results, EM data, open exceptions list)
authorised role and number of signatures
permitted dispositions (release, release with conditions, reject, hold)
engine_enforced_rules: all downstream steps are locked until an authorised QA disposition is signed
a gate cannot be released while a mandatory result is missing or failing without a documented QA decision on the related exception
rejection sets the intermediate status to rejected and blocks its use in any batch
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.22(a) (quality unit authority over in-process materials), 211.110(c), 211.192; EU GMP Chapter 1 and Chapter 5

name: Exception / event capture and deviation link
purpose: Record any departure from the MBR or any system-detected breach during execution, and connect it to the QMS deviation process.
config_options: exception categories and default routing
which categories allow the operator to continue vs require supervisor/QA acknowledgement first
mandatory fields per category
QMS integration mapping (create deviation, link existing)
engine_enforced_rules: system-detected breaches (limit, status override, time limit, interface failure, late entry) always create exceptions; they cannot be switched off per MBR
operators can raise an exception at any step
exceptions cannot be deleted, only dispositioned with reason and signature
batch record review/release is blocked while any exception is open
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.100(b), 211.192; EU GMP Chapter 1, Chapter 4 (deviations with signed authorisation); EU GMP Annex 16 (QP takes deviations into account)

name: Sub-procedure / library element call
purpose: Re-use an approved, parameterised sequence (library element, e.g. 'drain vessel', 'screen integrity check', 'PUPSIT') inside an MBR by reference.
config_options: referenced library element and version
parameter bindings for this call
instance name/label
equipment binding for the instance
engine_enforced_rules: the referenced version is frozen when the MBR is approved; execution never silently picks up a newer element version
where-used index is maintained; a new library version triggers impact assessment and, if adopted, new MBR versions
library elements have their own author/checker/approval lifecycle
parameters passed must satisfy the element's declared types, units and ranges at design time
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.100(a), 211.186; EU GMP Annex 11 section 10 (change and configuration management)

name: Conditional branch
purpose: Choose between alternative paths based on recorded data (e.g. LOD result, equipment type bound, product variant) or an explicit, authorised operator choice.
config_options: condition expressions over recorded data or parameters
branch targets and labels
operator-choice branch with allowed roles and mandatory reason
variant-driven branches resolved at record issuance (e.g. coating type for this product)
engine_enforced_rules: design-time check that conditions are exhaustive, non-overlapping and every branch is reachable
branch taken and its triggering data are recorded; untaken branches are marked not applicable by the system, not by users
variant branches resolved at issuance appear in the issued record as fixed, so reviewers see only the executed path plus the decision
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 11.10(f), 211.100(b), 211.186(b)(9); ISA-88 Part 2 PFC alternative branches

name: Loop / repeat-until
purpose: Repeat a sequence until an endpoint is reached (e.g. dry and test LOD until within limit, adjust pH until in range, re-sample coating weight gain) with a bounded number of iterations.
config_options: loop body
exit condition over recorded data
maximum iterations and/or maximum elapsed time
action when maximum reached (exception, QA gate)
engine_enforced_rules: every iteration's data is retained in order; iterations cannot overwrite each other
exceeding the maximum always raises an exception

loops are allowed only on parameters classified as process endpoints in the approved MBR; a loop whose exit condition is a release or acceptance test is rejected at design time (retesting of such results follows the OOS procedure instead of an MBR loop)
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.110, 211.192; FDA guidance Investigating OOS Test Results (Rev. 1, May 2022) which covers in-process lab tests and rejects averaging original with retest results

name: Parallel branches and synchronisation
purpose: Allow independent sequences to run concurrently (e.g. binder preparation while dry mixing; component preparation while compounding) and join them before a dependent step.
config_options: branches and their join type (all mandatory branches complete, or first-of)
location/resource constraints per branch
maximum skew allowed between branches (optional time limit)
engine_enforced_rules: a join step cannot start until the required branches are complete
shared equipment or material conflicts between branches are detected and blocked
each branch keeps its own attributable record and timestamps
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 11.10(f); ISA-88 Part 2 PFC simultaneous branches

name: Attachment and external evidence capture
purpose: Attach evidence that originates outside the eBR (instrument printouts, cycle reports, photos, supplier certificates) to a step.
config_options: permitted file types
required metadata (instrument ID, cycle/run number, time range)
capture method: electronic import from source system, scan of paper original, photo
reviewer role
engine_enforced_rules: attachments are hashed and immutable once saved; replacement is a new version with reason
where the source system keeps the original electronic data, the record links to or imports it rather than relying on a static PDF
scans of paper originals must be certified as true copies by an authorised person before the paper may be discarded
attachments appear in the review package; unreviewed attachments block review completion
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 11.10(b)-(c); EU GMP Annex 11 sections 7-8; FDA Data Integrity Q&A (2018) on true copies and dynamic vs static records

name: Yield and reconciliation
purpose: Compute actual yield vs theoretical at each appropriate stage and reconcile quantities (good output, samples, rejects, waste, retained, returned).
config_options: stage at which yield is computed
theoretical yield basis (formula total, actual charged quantities, or previous stage output)
categories counted in the balance
minimum and maximum percentage of theoretical yield
reconciliation tolerance for unit counts
engine_enforced_rules: an MBR cannot be approved if a configured yield stage lacks min/max limits
yield is computed by the validated engine from recorded quantities, then verified by one person (automated) or independently by a second person (manual)
result outside limits raises an exception that requires investigation before release
sample, waste and reject quantities recorded in other steps flow in automatically, not re-typed
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.103, 211.186(b)(7), 211.188(b), 211.192; EU GMP Chapter 5 (yields and reconciliation)

name: Printed packaging material / label issuance and reconciliation
purpose: Issue labels, cartons, leaflets and printed foils/lidding to a packaging batch under strict control and reconcile issued, used, destroyed, returned and damaged quantities.
config_options: items and approved artwork/version per market
issuance quantity rule (batch size plus allowance)
counting method (roll counter, weigh-count, manual count with verification)
reconciliation limits per item (narrow, based on historical data)
disposal rule for batch-coded surplus vs return of uncoded surplus
specimen capture (scanned or photographed printed specimen)
engine_enforced_rules: only released lots of the artwork version specified for this MBR/market can be issued (scan-verified)
the quantity balance must close; a discrepancy outside the preset limits raises an exception requiring investigation
batch-coded surplus must be recorded as destroyed (with witness); it cannot be returned to stock
specimens of all printed labelling used are captured in the record
an MBR cannot be approved with labelling steps lacking reconciliation limits
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.122, 211.125(c) (reconciliation with narrow preset limits based on historical data; investigation per 211.192), 211.130, 211.188(b) (labeling control records incl. specimens); EU GMP Chapter 5 (printed packaging materials)

name: Online variable-data printing and vision/code verification with challenge tests
purpose: Print lot, expiry (and serial) data on packs/labels from the batch record and prove the printing and inspection devices work, via start/periodic/end challenge tests.
config_options: variable data fields mapped from batch record (lot, expiry, manufacturing date, market-specific formats)
printer and camera/code reader device IDs
challenge test plan: triggers (start, after stoppage, periodic, end) and challenge types (wrong code, missing print, unreadable code, reject-bin verification)
first-print approval by second person or QA
engine_enforced_rules: variable data is transferred to the printer from the batch record; no manual keying at the device
printed data is compared to the batch record before running; mismatch blocks
challenge tests are mandatory at configured triggers; a failed or missed challenge stops the line step and raises an exception
device events (rejects, stops, parameter changes) are captured with timestamps
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.122(g) (special controls incl. 100% electronic verification for cut labeling), 211.130, 211.188(b); EU GMP Chapter 5 (on-line printing checks)

name: Serialisation and aggregation
purpose: Commission serial numbers onto saleable units and aggregate them to higher packaging levels for US DSCSA and EU FMD markets.
config_options: target market profile (US DSCSA product identifier with NDC/serial/lot/expiry; EU FMD unique identifier with GTIN/serial/batch/expiry plus anti-tampering device)
serial number source (Level 4/5 serialisation system)
aggregation hierarchy (unit, bundle, case, pallet)
sample and destroy handling (decommission reasons)
rework rules for re-packing
engine_enforced_rules: serials only from the authorised pool; every serial ends in a defined state (commissioned, decommissioned with reason, destroyed)
serial reconciliation closes before packaging completion
packaging batch cannot be released until serialisation data has been handed to the upstream system (and, for EU, confirmed uploaded to the repository as required by the process design)
anti-tampering device application is verified where the market requires it
regulatory_basis: US Drug Supply Chain Security Act (FD&C Act section 582); Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2016/161 (safety features)

name: Output/intermediate container registration and status labelling
purpose: Create uniquely identified containers of intermediate, bulk or finished product with tare/gross/net and quarantine status, and print their labels.
config_options: container types and tare source (weighed vs nominal)
sub-lot/container numbering scheme
label template per material type
initial status (default quarantine) and destination location
engine_enforced_rules: each container gets a system-unique ID and label printed from system data
net = gross - tare computed by the engine; quantities feed yield and inventory
status is quarantine until a QA disposition changes it; quarantined containers can't be consumed by a subsequent step unless the MBR explicitly allows use pending results under QA-approved conditions
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.80(d) (container identification and status), 211.105, 211.110(c); EU GMP Chapter 5 (labelling and status of containers)

name: Intermediate/bulk hold and transfer
purpose: Control storage and transfer of intermediates or bulk between stages or batches with validated hold times and storage conditions.
config_options: maximum hold time per material/stage (reference to hold-time study)
required storage conditions and location types
transfer approvals
re-test requirement if hold approaches limit
engine_enforced_rules: hold clock starts at the recorded completion event and is checked at the time of next use
use after expiry of hold is blocked unless QA dispositions an exception
storage location and condition excursions during the hold are pulled into the record
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.111; EU GMP Chapter 5; FDA aseptic processing guidance (2004) for sterile holds

name: Personnel qualification and training check
purpose: Ensure the person executing, verifying or approving a step is trained/qualified for it at that moment (the injectables edition adds gowning/APS qualification, see separate block).
config_options: training prerequisites per step type, MBR or equipment (curriculum items, SOP versions)
qualification types (e.g. equipment operator licence, visual inspector qualification)
grace rules (none by default)
presence log of persons in the room/line (optional)
engine_enforced_rules: qualification status is evaluated at action time against the training system of record; expired or missing qualification blocks the action
training on the effective MBR/SOP version is required where configured as a prerequisite; a new MBR version can trigger read-and-understand training before use
the qualification evidence (status snapshot) is stored with the action
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.25, 21 CFR 11.10(i); EU GMP Chapter 2

name: Section sign-off (production supervisor review)
purpose: Close a unit procedure/stage with a responsible-person review before the next stage or before QA review.
config_options: which sections require sign-off
reviewer role
checklist for the reviewer (exceptions acknowledged, attachments reviewed)
whether a performer in the section may also sign off
engine_enforced_rules: sign-off is possible only when all steps in the section are complete or system/authorised-NA, and all exceptions in the section are at least acknowledged
signature meaning 'reviewed' with timestamp; the reviewed content is hashed into the signature
a later correction to any step in the section invalidates the sign-off visibly and requires re-sign-off
regulatory_basis: EU GMP Chapter 4 (approval by the person responsible for processing operations); 21 CFR 211.188(b)(11) (persons directly supervising or checking)

name: Batch record review (review by exception) and disposition
purpose: End-of-batch QA review of the executed record focused on exceptions, followed by disposition (US quality unit approval; EU QP certification per Annex 16).
config_options: review stages and roles (production review, QA review, QP certification)
exception categories that must be individually reviewed (the mandatory set cannot be reduced)
audit-trail review scope for critical data (which data classes)
release interface to ERP
engine_enforced_rules: review cannot complete while steps are incomplete, exceptions open, attachments unreviewed, or linked deviations/QC results outstanding
the review-by-exception report is generated by the engine from all exceptions, corrections, late entries, overrides and critical audit-trail events; configuration cannot hide any of these
audit-trail entries for changes to critical data are presented for review before final approval
only users with the quality unit role (US) / QP role (EU) can sign disposition/certification; the person releasing is identified in the record
after disposition the record is locked; post-release corrections follow a controlled amendment process
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.22, 211.192; EU GMP Annex 16; EU GMP Annex 11 section 15 (only QPs certify via the system); FDA Data Integrity Q&A (2018) on audit trail review before final approval

name: Material return, waste and destruction record
purpose: Record unused material returned to stores, waste and rejected units, and destruction of materials, feeding reconciliation.
config_options: return reasons and destinations
waste categories
destruction witness requirement
engine_enforced_rules: returned material comes back with quarantine/appropriate status and its own label; quantities feed reconciliation automatically
destruction of batch-coded or rejected materials is witnessed by a second person
quantities cannot be edited after reconciliation without a correction record

name: Reprocessing / rework gate
purpose: Allow a batch or intermediate to be reprocessed only through an approved reprocessing procedure authorised by the quality unit.
config_options: library of approved reprocessing sub-procedures
entry conditions (e.g. linked investigation reference)
additional testing requirements
engine_enforced_rules: a reprocessing path can only be entered with a QA authorisation referencing an investigation/deviation
the reprocessing sub-procedure must itself be an approved master; ad-hoc steps are impossible
genealogy links the reprocessed material to the original batch and the record shows the rework path explicitly
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.115 (reprocessing procedures, quality unit review and approval); EU GMP Chapter 5

name: Packaging line inspection-device challenge (checkweigher, code reader, reject verification)
purpose: Verify at defined times that in-line inspection devices (checkweighers, code/vision readers, missing-leaflet detectors, reject gates) detect and reject defective units.
config_options: device list per line
challenge types and number of challenge pieces
frequency: start, after interruptions, periodic, end
acceptance: all challenge pieces rejected into the verified reject bin
engine_enforced_rules: challenge results recorded per device and time; failure stops the dependent step and raises an exception
output produced since the last successful challenge is flagged for evaluation if a challenge fails
missed scheduled challenges are exceptions at review
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.68(a) (routine checking of automatic equipment), 211.122(g), 211.130; EU GMP Chapter 5

name: Batch record issuance / order start
purpose: Create the executed batch record (ISA-88 control recipe) from an effective MBR for a specific batch: batch number, batch size, planned equipment, market/variant parameter set.
config_options: batch numbering scheme
allowed batch sizes/range and variant parameter set selection
planned start date and site/line
pre-issuance checks (material availability, equipment availability)
issuance approval (e.g. production planner plus QA for first batch after a change)
engine_enforced_rules: only an Effective MBR version valid for the site/product/batch size can be instantiated; its content hash is stored in the record
batch number is unique system-wide and cannot be reused, even for voided records
voiding a started record requires QA approval and the voided record is retained and linked to its replacement
scaled quantities are computed at issuance and displayed with the calculation trace
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.186, 211.188(a); EU GMP Chapter 4 (batch processing record based on current approved instructions; method avoids transcription errors); FDA Data Integrity Q&A (2018) on control of blank forms/records

name: Equipment cleaning execution record
purpose: Execute and record cleaning of equipment/rooms (between batches, product changeover, campaign end) as a procedure linked to equipment status and logbooks.
config_options: cleaning procedure per equipment class and cleaning type (minor/major, product-specific)
cleaning agents, concentrations, temperatures, times; CIP cycle import
visual inspection checklist and verification
sampling for residues/micro (swab/rinse) with LIMS link
clean-hold time to assign
engine_enforced_rules: completion sets equipment to 'clean' with a clean-hold expiry only after verification and required results
campaign length and dirty-hold limits are enforced from recorded use events
cleaning records are linked into the equipment logbook and to the batches that follow
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.67, 211.182; EU GMP Chapter 3 and Chapter 5; EU GMP Annex 15 (cleaning validation)

name: Sub-batch split and merge (genealogy)
purpose: Split a batch into sub-lots (e.g. several granulation sub-batches, several lyophiliser or steriliser loads, several packaging runs) and merge sub-lots into one downstream batch, keeping full genealogy.
config_options: allowed split/merge points in the flow
maximum number of sub-lots and naming rule
rules for merging (all sub-lots must be released/passed IPC, same MBR version, within hold time)
quantity allocation and reconciliation per sub-lot
engine_enforced_rules: every sub-lot has its own ID, record section and quantities; genealogy links are system-generated
merge is blocked if any sub-lot has open exceptions, failed IPC or expired hold unless QA dispositions
sub-lot quantities reconcile to the parent batch
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.188(b), 211.103, 211.111; EU GMP Chapter 4 and Chapter 5
